message.content:
The fog rolled in like a gray tide, swallowing the cliffs of Blackwood Point until only the rhythmic *thump-thump* of the waves remained. Elias Thorne, the lighthouse keeper, wiped the condensation from the glass of the lantern room. He was a man of routine, of oil and wick, of silence and salt. For thirty years, he had watched the horizon, expecting nothing but the occasional fishing trawler or the ghostly shimmer of a distant ship.

But today, the mail boat had brought something different.

It wasn’t a package, nor a bill. It was a single envelope, yellowed and brittle, smelling faintly of ozone and old paper. There was no return address, only his name, written in a handwriting that looked disturbingly like his own, but sharper, more hurried.

Elias’s hands trembled as he broke the seal. Inside was a single sheet of paper, dated October 14, 2045.

*Elias,*

*If you are reading this, the storm is coming. Not the wind, not the rain, but the silence. The grid fails at 3:17 AM. The backup generator will kick in, but it will fail at 3:22. You have five minutes. Do not trust the automated system. It will try to shut down the main beam to conserve power. You must manually override the switch in the basement. It is rusted shut. Use the crowbar from the tool shed. If you fail, the ships in the harbor will not see the light. They will crash. I know because I was there. I was the one who couldn’t do it in time. I am writing this from the future, where the sea is quiet and the light is gone. Save them, Elias. Save yourself.*

*— E.T.*

Elias stared at the letter, his heart hammering against his ribs. It was a prank. It had to be. Who else knew his name? Who else lived in this isolated tower? He looked at the clock on the wall. 2:45 AM. The fog outside was thickening, turning the world into a void.

He folded the letter and shoved it into his pocket. He told himself he would throw it in the fire. He told himself it was madness. But as he descended the spiral stairs, his feet felt heavy, as if the stone itself was pulling him down.
